design.affected_system: air-quality surveillance, exposure reduction, and respiratory-health response
alternatives: rank verified high-consequence candidates for air-exposure reduction and health-protection portfolio
select a risk-, equity-, and lifecycle-balanced portfolio for air-exposure reduction and health-protection portfolio
pair source, exposure, equity, and lifecycle project optimization with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Monitor data retain calibration, siting, uptime, and spatial-representativeness metadata.
Exposure, diagnosis, care use, and service complaints are not interchangeable outcomes.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: fund only already-committed work for air-exposure reduction and health-protection portfolio.

constraints.description: The air-quality exposure and respiratory health prioritize must respect declared capital, operating, maintenance, and delivery budgets.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: environmental health director and air-quality program lead
design.decision_question: Which source-control, building, monitoring, and health-protection measures should be funded first?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The air-quality exposure and respiratory health prioritize must respect declared capital, operating, maintenance, and delivery budgets.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for air-exposure reduction and health-protection portfolio passes documented checks for cost, benefit, service life, dependencies, deliverability, and maintenance burden.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: source, exposure, equity, and lifecycle project optimization

design.intended_claim: A versioned prioritize design for comparing declared alternatives affecting air-exposure reduction and health-protection portfolio, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: distributional gap in population-weighted exposure above health-protection thresholds
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not report modeled exposure reduction as avoided disease or realized emissions compliance.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for air-exposure reduction and health-protection portfolio passes documented checks for cost, benefit, service life, dependencies, deliverability, and maintenance burden.

design.title: Prioritize air-exposure reduction investments
transportability_risks: Pollutant mixtures, indoor infiltration, source profiles, coding, and monitor coverage differ.
Modeled concentration may not represent personal exposure.

family.affected_system: air-quality surveillance, exposure reduction, and respiratory-health response
claim_boundary: Area exposure, service, and vulnerability records do not diagnose individuals or prove harm.
Operational allocations are proposed planning outputs, not delivered clinical or social services.
Health-effect claims require outcome panels, identification, privacy, and external review.
family.decision_owner: environmental health director and air-quality program lead
family.description: Eight decisions for exposure-health diagnosis, syndrome forecasting, mitigation portfolios, monitor siting, protection allocation, alert timing, pollution stress, and program evaluation.
family.title: Air-quality exposure and respiratory health

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
